authority.role: Architecture, interface governance, compatibility and evidence control plane only
authority.implementation_rule: This draft does not transfer canonical implementation ownership and does not authorize implementation or merge.

provenance.note: Draft created from current PR metadata and architecture constraints. Contracts require validation against canonical source repositories and their exact HEADs.

contracts.name: A-TownChain Product Boundary
contracts.canonical_path: components/{algorithm,vm,node,transaction and state modules} (each subcomponent retains its own canonical path)
consumers: Aurora AI only through explicitly approved transaction APIs

inputs.name: transaction envelope
inputs.constraints: TX-V2 format must be specified by the normative standards and canonical implementation; reject legacy signing domain ATC-TX-DOMAIN and atc-tx.v1.

inputs.name: execution request
inputs.constraints: Deterministic encoding; bounded lengths and resource budgets; no implicit defaults for consensus-critical fields.

outputs.name: execution result
outputs.constraints: Deterministic success result or typed error; no silent partial success.

outputs.name: state/receipt
outputs.constraints: Commit only according to finalized normative state-transition and transaction rules.

error_semantics: Malformed or non-canonical encoding is rejected before state mutation.
Signature, authorization, replay, resource-limit and version failures are explicit typed errors.
Consensus-critical nondeterminism is a hard failure, not a fallback.
security_requirements: Canonical transaction signing and verification rules must be versioned in atc-standards.
No AI caller receives implicit signing, wallet or consensus authority.
VM and node resource limits must be enforced at trust boundaries.
compatibility_rules: Versioned wire and ABI contracts; reject unsupported major versions.
Cross-language golden vectors required for encoding, signing preimages, transaction IDs and invalid inputs.
ATCB versus ATC1 magic remains BLOCKED until a normative decision is approved.
tests: Golden vectors for valid and invalid TX-V2 transactions
open_blockers: IF-002: ATCB vs ATC1 bytecode magic unresolved.
IF-003: consensus selection, finality, quorum and fork-choice lack an approved versioned normative decision.
SCR-0128 ATC-VM-ABI stage remains separately BLOCKED.

contracts.name: GlobusOS / ShivaCore System Boundary
contracts.canonical_path: modules/atc-shivacore/kernel/ (ShivaCore canonical kernel); service and HAL paths remain owned by their canonical GlobusOS modules
consumers: Aurora Runtime through explicitly granted service capabilities

inputs.name: system call or IPC request
inputs.constraints: Caller identity, capability, message length and operation budget validated before dispatch.

inputs.name: resource request
inputs.constraints: Explicit authority for memory, device, IPC and scheduling resources; no ambient authority.

outputs.name: IPC/system call result
outputs.constraints: Caller-visible success/failure with ownership and lifetime semantics.

outputs.name: resource handle
outputs.constraints: Least authority, explicit revocation/lifetime rules and no privilege escalation.

error_semantics: Permission/capability denial is explicit and fail-closed.
Invalid ABI version, malformed message and resource exhaustion return typed errors.
Driver or service failure must not be reported as successful completion.
security_requirements: Rust no_std kernel/TCB boundary; minimize privileged code.
Validate bounds, ownership, provenance and capability rights at every crossing.
Secure Boot/TPM/TEE claims require separate exact-hardware evidence; do not infer them from build success.
compatibility_rules: Kernel ABI, IPC schema and HAL contracts are separately versioned.
Breaking ABI changes require explicit migration/version negotiation.
Userspace and AI services cannot bypass kernel capability checks.
tests: QEMU and physical-hardware evidence tracked separately
open_blockers: Exact canonical kernel/HAL/service source bindings and interface versions still require reconciliation.
Secure Boot and full hardware/userspace readiness are not established by this contract draft.

contracts.name: Aurora AI Authority and Runtime Boundary
contracts.canonical_path: Aurora AI Control Plane / Agent Platform / Runtime canonical paths to be verified against current repository tree
consumers: A-TownChain transaction APIs via policy-gated adapters

inputs.name: intent
inputs.constraints: Normalize and classify; caller identity and policy context must be attached.

inputs.name: tool request
inputs.constraints: Tool capability, scope, arguments and resource budget must be validated before execution.

outputs.name: plan/action result
outputs.constraints: Record selected tools, policy decisions, execution status and evidence references.

outputs.name: approval request
outputs.constraints: Required for wallet, transaction, privileged system and other configured critical actions.

error_semantics: Policy denial, missing capability, timeout, sandbox violation and tool failure are distinct errors.
No silent fallback from denied privileged action to a broader-capability tool.
Partial agent execution is reported as partial, not complete.
security_requirements: Control Plane enforces policy, capability and audit before Runtime dispatch.
Tools execute in least-privilege sandboxed environments.
Wallet/transaction actions require explicit approval path and canonical transaction validation.
Model output is untrusted input; it cannot grant authority or override policy.
compatibility_rules: Agent/tool schemas and runtime ABI are versioned.
Tool changes require compatibility tests and audit-field preservation.
Model-provider changes must not alter authorization semantics.
open_blockers: Canonical Aurora AI source paths and current HEAD SHA must be confirmed from the live repository tree.
No model output may be treated as authorization evidence.

contracts.name: Product-Interoperability Governance Boundary
contracts.canonical_path: atc-standards normative registry; a-townchain-ecosystem derived catalog, dependency graph and evidence reports

inputs.name: interface proposal
inputs.constraints: Must identify producer, consumer, owner, canonical path, schemas, errors, security, compatibility and tests.

inputs.name: evidence bundle
inputs.constraints: Full lowercase 40-character SHA plus run/job/step, terminal conclusion, exit code and immutable log/artifact references.

outputs.name: normative contract decision
outputs.constraints: Only atc-standards owns normative decisions; ecosystem mirrors are derived references.

outputs.name: reconciliation result
outputs.constraints: Every source candidate mapped, explicitly excluded with reason, or retained as UNRESOLVED/BLOCKED.

error_semantics: Missing, stale or incomplete evidence fails closed.
Conflicting SSOT ownership remains UNRESOLVED until explicitly adjudicated.
Unknown consensus or ABI semantics remain BLOCKED.
security_requirements: One canonical implementation owner per capability.
No duplicated production implementation in the ecosystem control plane.
Full SHA and exact workflow evidence required for VERIFIED claims.
compatibility_rules: Semantic versioning and deprecation policy required per public contract.
Dependency graph edges reference interface IDs and versions.
Source catalogs preserve original IDs and source provenance; duplicates are not silently merged.
open_blockers: Current source-symbol reconciliation gate fails on unbound candidates; exact terminal counts must be read from the uploaded artifact before triage.
The ecosystem registry is a governance projection, not an implementation SSOT.

special_blockers.rule: ATC-VM-ABI is a separate open stage; this draft does not settle its ABI or bytecode magic.
Consensus selection, finality, quorum and fork-choice require approved versioned normative decisions.

acceptance_gates: Each contract validated against current canonical source tree and exact full source SHA.
Each interface has a schema, error semantics, security requirements, compatibility rules and passing contract tests.
Catalog/census mismatches are mapped or reasonedly excluded; unresolved entries remain UNRESOLVED/BLOCKED.
No functional verification claim without exact-SHA Run→Job→Step→exit-code/log/artifact evidence.
